title: Journey - Walking Through Grief - Day 3: Comfort that lasts

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, slow and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Walking Through Grief. <short pause> This is day three, Comfort That Lasts. <short pause> Walk with me... remember with me. <short pause> Today there is nothing to carry, and nothing to give. <short pause> Only something to receive, if you can.

Paul knew what it was to be crushed. <short pause> He once told his friends that the weight had been far beyond his strength, until he despaired of life itself. <short pause> He doesn't hurry past that. <short pause> And in the same letter, he gives God this name, in Second Corinthians chapter one, verses three and four.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort; <short pause> Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.

parts.style: tender, soft, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: One day, you may sit beside someone else who is grieving, and know not to say very much. <short pause> But that is not your task today. <short pause> Your loss didn't happen to make you useful. <short pause> The comfort comes first... <short pause> and it is for you.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: So let a little of it in. <short pause> Think of one kindness that has reached you. <short pause> A meal at the door. A hand on your back. A message that needed no answer. <short pause> If you can't find one, rest your own hand over your heart... and let God begin there.

parts.style: prayerful, slow, soft but clearly spoken
parts.text: God of all comfort, I am tired of being strong. <short pause> Come as softly as You need to. <short pause> Send me people who can stay, and help me to let them. <short pause> Comfort me. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, steady, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: The next time someone offers you something small, you could try saying yes. <short pause> A cup of tea. A ride. Ten minutes of company. <short pause> And under your breath, the prayer... <short pause> comfort me. <short pause> Go gently.
